newsitem.title: USA: New York Mayor sues U.S. on immigration.
newsitem.headline: New York Mayor sues U.S. on immigration.

text.p: Mayor Rudolph Giuliani filed suit against the federal government Friday, challenging new immigration and welfare laws as exceeding federal power.

The lawsuit filed in Manhattan federal court said that provisions of new federal policies were unconstitutional, and specifically those allowing city employees to turn in illegal immigrants who apply for health care, public education or police protection.
The New York City lawsuit, in which pro-immigration Mayor Giuliani was named as a plaintiff, said that the laws were unconstitutional because they violated the 10th Amendment.
The amendment gives the states all powers not expressly granted to the federal government.
Provisions of the Welfare Reform Act and the Immigration Reform Act would overturn a New York City executive order that bars city employees from reporting illegal immigrants.

"The reasons for this policy are evident: undocumented aliens who are witnesses to or victims of crime must not be deterred from coming forward for fear of deportation, nor should undocumented aliens who are infected with contagious diseases be deterred from seeking treatment, nor should undocumented alien children be afraid to attend public schools and forfeit their right to an education," the court papers said.
